In six-dimensional [[geometry]], a '''pentellated 6-simplex''' is a convex [[uniform 6-polytope]] with 5th order [[Truncation (geometry)|truncations]] of the regular [[6-simplex]].

There are unique 10 degrees of pentellations of the 6-simplex with permutations of truncations, cantellations, runcinations, and sterications. The simple '''pentellated 6-simplex''' is also called an '''expanded 6-simplex''', constructed by an [[Expansion (geometry)|expansion]] operation applied to the regular [[6-simplex]]. The highest form, the ''pentisteriruncicantitruncated 6-simplex'', is called an ''omnitruncated 6-simplex'' with all of the nodes ringed.
{{Clear}}

=== Alternate names ===
* Expanded 6-simplex
* Small terated tetradecapeton (Acronym: {{not a typo|staf}}) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/staf.htm (x3o3o3o3o3x - staf)]}}

=== Cross-sections ===
The maximal cross-section of the pentellated 6-simplex with a 5-dimensional hyperplane is a [[Stericated 5-simplexes#Stericated 5-simplex|stericated hexateron]]. This cross-section divides the pentellated 6-simplex into two [[Cupola (geometry)#Hypercupolas|hexateral hypercupolas]] consisting of 7 [[5-simplex]]es, 21 [[5-cell prism]]s and 35 [[Duoprism|Tetrahedral-Triangular duoprisms]] each.

=== Coordinates ===
The vertices of the ''pentellated 6-simplex'' can be positioned in 7-space as permutations of (0,1,1,1,1,1,2). This construction is based on [[Facet (geometry)|facets]] of the [[pentellated 7-orthoplex]].

A second construction in 7-space, from the center of a [[rectified 7-orthoplex]] is given by coordinate permutations of:
: (1,-1,0,0,0,0,0)

=== Root vectors ===
Its 42 vertices represent the root vectors of the [[simple Lie group]] A<sub>6</sub>. It is the [[vertex figure]] of the [[6-simplex honeycomb]].

=== Images ===
{{6-simplex2 Coxeter plane graphs|t05|150}}

=== Configuration ===
This [[Regular 4-polytope#As configurations|configuration matrix]] represents the expanded 6-simplex, with 12 permutations of elements. The rows and columns correspond to vertices, edges, faces, cells, 4-faces and 5-faces. The diagonal numbers say how many of each element occur in the whole polytope. The nondiagonal numbers say how many of the column's element occur in or at the row's element.{{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/staf.htm (x3o3o3o3o3x - staf)]}}

The '''omnitruncated 6-simplex''' has 5040 [[vertex (geometry)|vertices]], 15120 [[Edge (geometry)|edge]]s, 16800 [[Face (geometry)|faces]] (4200 [[hexagon]]s and 1260 [[Square (geometry)|squares]]), 8400 [[Cell (mathematics)|cells]], 1806 4-faces, and 126 5-faces. With 5040 vertices, it is the largest of 35 [[uniform 6-polytope]]s generated from the regular [[6-simplex]].

=== Alternate names ===
* Pentisteriruncicantitruncated 6-simplex (Johnson's [[omnitruncation]] for 6-polytopes)
* Omnitruncated heptapeton
* Great terated tetradecapeton (Acronym: gotaf) (Jonathan Bowers){{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/gotaf.htm (x3x3x3x3x3x - gotaf)]}}

=== Permutohedron and related tessellation ===
The omnitruncated 6-simplex is the [[permutohedron]] of order 7. The omnitruncated 6-simplex is a [[zonotope]], the [[Minkowski sum]] of seven line segments parallel to the seven lines through the origin and the seven vertices of the 6-simplex.

Like all uniform omnitruncated n-simplices, the '''omnitruncated 6-simplex''' can [[tessellate]] space by itself, in this case 6-dimensional space with three facets around each hypercell. It has [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] of {{CDD|branch_11|3ab|nodes_11|3ab|nodes_11|split2|node_1}}.

=== Coordinates ===
The vertices of the ''omnitruncated 6-simplex'' can be most simply positioned in 7-space as permutations of (0,1,2,3,4,5,6). This construction is based on [[Facet (geometry)|facets]] of the [[pentisteriruncicantitruncated 7-orthoplex]], t<sub>0,1,2,3,4,5</sub>{3<sup>5</sup>,4}, {{CDD|node|4|node_1|3|node_1|3|node_1|3|node_1|3|node_1|3|node_1}}.

=== Images ===
{{6-simplex2 Coxeter plane graphs|t012345|150}}

=== Configuration ===
This [[Regular 4-polytope#As configurations|configuration matrix]] represents the omnitruncated 6-simplex, with 35 permutations of elements. The rows and columns correspond to vertices, edges, faces, cells, 4-faces and 5-faces. The diagonal numbers say how many of each element occur in the whole polytope. The nondiagonal numbers say how many of the column's element occur in or at the row's element.{{sfn|Klitzing|at=[https://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/gotaf.htm (x3x3x3x3x3x - gotaf)]}}

=== Full snub 6-simplex ===
The '''full snub 6-simplex''' or '''omnisnub 6-simplex''', defined as an [[Alternation (geometry)|alternation]] of the omnitruncated 6-simplex is not uniform, but it can be given Coxeter diagram {{CDD|node_h|3|node_h|3|node_h|3|node_h|3|node_h|3|node_h}} and [[Coxeter notation|symmetry]] {{brackets|3,3,3,3,3}}<sup>+</sup>, and constructed from 14 [[Stericated 5-simplexes#Full snub 5-simplex|snub 5-simplex]]es, 42 snub 5-cell antiprisms, 70 3-s{3,4} duoantiprisms, and 2520 irregular [[5-simplex]]es filling the gaps at the deleted vertices.

== Related uniform 6-polytopes ==
The pentellated 6-simplexes are in a set of 35 [[uniform 6-polytope]]s based on the [3,3,3,3,3] [[Coxeter group]], all shown here in A<sub>6</sub> [[Coxeter plane]] [[orthographic projection]]s.
{{Heptapeton family}}
